source_cell: Fig. 1A, y axis 'Shoot Weight (g)', bars contr1, Myco, contr2, Ozor (left to right), upper cap of each bar; RKN-inoculated plants harvested 2 months after inoculation.
source_quote: Figure 1. Plant growth (A,B) and infection indicators (C,D) of tomato plants harvested 2 months after inoculation with the root-knot nematode M. incognita. Treatments with 0.25 g Myco and 0.08 g Ozor g-1 plant fresh weight were carried out 5 days before nematode inoculation. Infection level was estimated by the number of sedentary forms (SFs) developed in each root system and by the reproduction potential (RP) of the nematode population. Means +/- standard deviations for treated (Myco, Ozor) and untreated (contr1, contr2) plants were separated by a paired t-test (* p < 0.05; ** p < 0.01).

source_cell: Figure 1 panel D, PDF p.3, y-axis RP (printed ticks 0, 50, 100, 150), bars contr1, Myco, contr2, Ozor; harvest 2 months after inoculation per caption
source_quote: Figure 1. Plant growth (A,B) and infection indicators (C,D) of tomato plants harvested 2 months after inoculation with the root-knot nematode M. incognita. Treatments with 0.25 g Myco and 0.08 g Ozor g−1 plant fresh weight were carried out 5 days before nematode inoculation. Infection level was estimated by the number of sedentary forms (SFs) developed in each root system and by the reproduction potential (RP) of the nematode population. Means ± standard deviations for treated (Myco, Ozor) and untreated (contr1, contr2) plants were separated by a paired t-test (* p < 0.05; ** p < 0.01).

Treatments with 0.25 g Myco g-1 plant fresh weight were carried out 5 days before randomly locating plants in the infested glasshouse. Detected growth factors (A) were shoot (SW) and root weights (RW). Infection factors (B) were the number of leaves carrying at least one mine per plantand the number of galleries present on each infested leaf. Means ± standard deviations for treated (Myco) and untreated (Contr) plants were separated by a paired t-test (* p < 0.05).
